features.description: Review native inputs and source evidence before generating. Examples are illustrative and require your review.

fields.label: Text1
presets: The campus garden collected rainwater in two storage barrels. Volunteers measured soil moisture each Friday and watered only when the top layer was dry. After eight weeks, weekly water use fell from 120 to 85 liters; the team recorded rainfall to help explain the change.

Our library extended evening hours during the exam period. We surveyed 46 students, of whom 31 preferred a quiet study space after 8 p.m. Attendance rose during the first week, but the short trial does not establish whether the effect will persist.

A neighborhood repair workshop fixed 18 bicycles in April. Residents supplied replacement parts, while volunteers taught brake adjustment and tire repair. The next workshop will track how many bicycles are still in use after three months.

fields.label: Text2
presets: Volunteers in the university garden stored rainfall in a pair of barrels. Every Friday they checked soil moisture before watering. Water use dropped from 120 to 85 liters per week over an eight-week period, though rainfall also changed.

The library stayed open later for exams. A survey of 46 students found that 31 wanted quiet evening study space. More students attended the first week; a longer observation period is needed to assess the lasting impact.

In April, a community event repaired eighteen bikes using parts brought by residents. Volunteers demonstrated tire repairs and brake adjustments. Organizers plan to ask participants whether the bikes remain in use three months later.
